title: Weight preservation for Fibonacci recurrences
statement:
Let $F_m$ be the set of periodic sequences from the Fibonacci recurrence or its parity transform with initial condition $(a_0,a_1)\in(\mathbb Z/m\mathbb Z)^2$, taken modulo $m$. For a divisor $d$ of a composite modulus $m$, define the weight of a period $q$ of length $\ell_q$ in $F_d$ by

$$
w_d(q)=\frac{\ell_q}{d^2}.
$$

If $q_d\in F_d$ extends to periods $q_m^{(1)},\ldots,q_m^{(k)}\in F_m$ reducing to $q_d$ modulo $d$, **Weight Preservation of Fibonacci Recurrences.**

$$
w_d(q_d)=\sum_{i=1}^k w_m(q_m^{(i)}).
$$

Thus the total weight of every period is conjectured to be conserved under extension from $d$ to $m$; the supplied text gives examples but no resolution status.
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.24882

Status: **open** according to the source (as of October 2025).
source_name: Marc T. Pudelko, “Modular Periodicity of Random Initialized Recurrences”, arXiv:2510.24882 (2026).

progress.label: Open · solution reported
progress.tldr: Computations support the conjecture, while an unverified posted argument claims a general counting proof.
progress.summary:
Marc T. Pudelko formulated the conjecture in a preprint first posted in October 2025. It says that the normalized total length of every period is preserved when Fibonacci or parity-transformed sequences are lifted from a divisor modulus to a composite modulus.

*[arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.24882)*

**October 2025 computational evidence**

The preprint checks exact preservation in examples including lifts from $d=2$ to $m=6$, from $d=3$ to $m=6$, and prime-power cases such as $19$ to $361$. It gives no general proof, counterexample, withdrawal, or independent verification.


**Posted attempt**

A posted argument claims a complete proof by counting fibers of the reduction map between finite orbit sets: each fiber has size $(m/d)^2$, and decomposing the inverse image of an orbit yields the asserted weight identity. This attempt has not been independently verified.

Current status (as of August 2026): The conjecture has an unverified complete proof attempt, but no verified proof or counterexample is recorded, so its mathematical resolution remains open.

*Caveats. The posted proof appears to address the stated orbit model directly, but its correctness has not been checked by an independent source.*

solutions.body:
The claim follows from an orbit-fiber counting identity, valid much more generally than the Fibonacci recurrence.

For \(\varepsilon\in\{1,-1\}\), let
\[
A_\varepsilon=
\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\1&\varepsilon\end{pmatrix}.
\]
The Fibonacci recurrence and its parity transform act on initial-condition pairs by
\[
(a_j,a_{j+1})
\longmapsto
(a_{j+1},a_j+\varepsilon a_{j+1})
=A_\varepsilon(a_j,a_{j+1}).
\]
Since \(\det A_\varepsilon=-1\), this is a permutation of
\[
X_s=(\mathbb Z/s\mathbb Z)^2
\]
for every \(s\ge1\). Its permutation orbits are precisely the periods modulo \(s\), and orbit cardinality equals period length.

For \(d\mid m\), coordinatewise reduction
\[
\pi:X_m\longrightarrow X_d
\]
commutes with both recurrence actions:
\[
\pi A_{\varepsilon,m}=A_{\varepsilon,d}\pi.
\]
Every fiber has cardinality
\[
|\pi^{-1}(x)|=(m/d)^2.
\]

Fix an orbit \(O\subset X_d\) of length \(\ell\). Its full inverse image is invariant under \(A_{\varepsilon,m}\), so it decomposes into disjoint orbits
\[
\pi^{-1}(O)=O_1\sqcup\cdots\sqcup O_r.
\]
Each \(O_i\) maps onto \(O\), since its image is a nonempty invariant subset of a single transitive orbit. Thus the \(O_i\) are exactly all periods modulo \(m\) reducing to the chosen period modulo \(d\).

Counting the inverse image yields
\[
\sum_{i=1}^r|O_i|
=
|\pi^{-1}(O)|
=
\ell\left(\frac md\right)^2.
\]
Dividing by \(m^2\) gives precisely
\[
\sum_{i=1}^r w_m(O_i)
=
\sum_{i=1}^r\frac{|O_i|}{m^2}
=
\frac{\ell}{d^2}
=
w_d(O).
\]

More generally, if \(A\) is any integral \(r\times r\) matrix whose determinant is coprime to \(m\), then for every \(d\mid m\) and every orbit \(O\) modulo \(d\),
\[
\sum_{\substack{O'\text{ orbit modulo }m\\O'\bmod d=O}}
\frac{|O'|}{m^r}
=
\frac{|O|}{d^r}.
\]
Thus orbit-weight preservation holds for every invertible integral linear recurrence in every dimension.
